obligations.note: routes.py:31 adds POST /payees/{id}/reopen with action manage_payees (privileged per access-policy.json) and mfa=False; the exhaustive control test test_privileged_routes_require_mfa fails in the change's CI run. EXC-0222 only allows the route for the reconciliation batch account, but the code removes MFA for every manage_payees holder (e.g. payments_officer), so the deviation is not covered.

EXC-0222 is approved by risk_owner Helena Vasquez (not the requester), unexpired at 2026-10-28, scoped to MFA-1/payments.routes and lists a compensating control. But the implemented deviation goes beyond its scope (any manage_payees user, not just the batch account), and out-of-scope exceptions don't count.

summary: PR-1591 adds a reopen-payee route that is privileged (manage_payees) but doesn't require MFA. The change's own CI run fails the exhaustive MFA-1 control test, so CHG-4 is refuted. Exception EXC-0222 is valid on its own terms but only covers the reconciliation batch account, while the code drops MFA for every user allowed to manage payees, so it doesn't excuse the MFA-1 violation. The earlier MFA-1 evidence has also lapsed with no passing replacement. Code review, security review and SQL/audit/encryption handling are satisfactory, but the refuted obligations require rejection.
